title: Taiwan's Lawmakers Clash Over a Nuclear Power Referendum
summaryZh: 11/28核能公投前，藍綠立委電視交鋒
summaryHi: 28 नवंबर के परमाणु जनमत संग्रह से पहले ताइवान के सांसदों में टीवी पर तीखी बहस
summaryEs: Legisladores de Taiwán chocan en televisión antes del referéndum nuclear del 28 de noviembre
summaryJa: 11月28日の原発国民投票を前に、台湾の与野党議員がテレビで激論
summaryKo: 11월 28일 원전 국민투표 앞두고 대만 여야 의원들 TV 토론서 격돌
summaryEn: Taiwan's ruling and opposition lawmakers clash on TV ahead of the 28 November nuclear power referendum
paragraphs: Taiwan's ruling and opposition lawmakers clashed on 12 November during a televised presentation about a nuclear power referendum. The vote will take place on 28 November, alongside the nationwide local elections.

The legislature approved the referendum in August by 59 votes to 51, following a proposal from the main opposition party, the Kuomintang (KMT). Voters will be asked whether they support using nuclear energy to boost the economy and ending the 'nuclear-free homeland' policy.

KMT legislator Niu Hsu-ting urged a yes vote, arguing that nuclear and renewable energy should be developed side by side. He said chipmakers and artificial intelligence firms depend on stable baseload power. He also warned that imported gas could be cut off by a maritime blockade, while nuclear fuel is easier to stockpile.

Chen Pei-yu of the governing Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) argued that the referendum was unnecessary, since lawmakers could amend the existing law. She said any return to nuclear power depends on three conditions: safety, a workable plan for waste and social consensus. She added that the vote would cost taxpayers around NT$800 million.
Taiwan has produced no nuclear power since its last reactor shut down in May 2025. Four further presentations on energy policy are scheduled for later this month.
Taiwan will vote on nuclear power on 28 November. On the same day, people will also vote in local elections.

On 12 November, lawmakers talked about the vote on TV. Niu Hsu-ting is from the KMT, the biggest opposition party. He wants people to vote yes. He says Taiwan needs nuclear power and also clean power from the sun and wind. Chip and AI companies need a lot of stable electricity.
Chen Pei-yu is from the DPP, the ruling party. She wants people to vote no. She says lawmakers can change the law without a vote. She also says the vote will cost about NT$800 million.
Taiwan has used no nuclear power since May 2025. In a vote in 2025, more people said yes, but not enough people voted. There will be four more TV talks about energy.

他希望大家投同意票。
他說台灣需要核能，也需要來自太陽和風的乾淨能源。
晶片和人工智慧公司需要大量穩定的電力。
陳培瑜來自執政黨民進黨。
她希望大家投不同意票。

paragraphs: Taiwan will hold a referendum on nuclear power on 28 November, the same day as the country's local elections. On 12 November, lawmakers from the two main parties argued about it in the first of several TV presentations.

Niu Hsu-ting of the opposition Kuomintang (KMT) asked voters to say yes. He said Taiwan should develop nuclear power and renewable energy together. In his view, chipmakers and AI companies need stable power all day and night. He also warned that Taiwan buys most of its fuel from abroad, and that gas ships could be stopped in a blockade.

Chen Pei-yu of the ruling Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) disagreed. She said the referendum was not needed because lawmakers could simply change the law. The government has three conditions for nuclear power: it must be safe, there must be a plan for nuclear waste, and society must agree.
Chen added that the economy has kept growing without nuclear power. She also said the referendum would cost taxpayers about NT$800 million.

Taiwan's last nuclear reactor stopped in May 2025. A referendum that year got more yes votes than no votes, but too few people took part for it to pass. Four more presentations are planned this month.
sentZh: 台灣將在11月28日舉行核能公投，與全國地方選舉同一天。
11月12日，兩大黨的立委在數場電視發表會的第一場中為此爭論。
在野黨國民黨的牛煦庭呼籲選民投同意票。
他說台灣應該同時發展核能和再生能源。
他認為，晶片製造商和人工智慧公司需要全天候穩定的電力。
他也警告，台灣大部分燃料從國外購買，而天然氣船可能在封鎖中被攔阻。
執政黨民進黨的陳培瑜則不同意。
她說公投沒有必要，因為立委可以直接修法。
政府對核能有三個條件：必須安全、必須有核廢料處理計畫，以及社會必須有共識。
陳培瑜補充說，沒有核能，經濟依然持續成長。
她也說這次公投將花費納稅人約新台幣8億元。
台灣最後一座核反應爐在2025年5月停止運轉。
當年的一次公投同意票多於不同意票，但參與的人太少，因此沒有通過。
本月還計畫舉辦四場發表會。

paragraphs: With just over two weeks until Taiwan votes on the future of nuclear power, lawmakers from the ruling and opposition camps traded sharp arguments on 12 November in the first of a series of televised presentations. The referendum will be held on 28 November, coinciding with local elections across the country.

The question, put forward by the opposition Kuomintang (KMT) and passed by the legislature in August by a narrow 59-51 margin, asks whether voters back reviving the economy with nuclear energy and scrapping the long-standing 'nuclear-free homeland' policy.

Making the case for a yes vote, KMT legislator Niu Hsu-ting insisted that nuclear and renewable sources should be expanded in parallel. He contended that the semiconductor and AI sectors require reliable baseload electricity, and that heavy dependence on imported fossil fuels leaves Taiwan exposed both to volatile global prices and to a potential naval blockade.

Chen Pei-yu of the governing Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) countered that the vote was redundant, as legislators could simply amend existing legislation. She reiterated the government's three preconditions for any nuclear revival, namely safety, a viable waste solution and social consensus, and pointed out that the economy had continued to grow throughout the energy transition. The exercise, she noted, would cost around NT$800 million.
Taiwan has generated no nuclear power since May 2025, when its final reactor went offline. A referendum held that year won more yes than no votes but fell short of the required turnout threshold.
sentZh: 距離台灣就核能前途投票只剩兩週多，朝野陣營的立委11月12日在一系列電視發表會的首場中激烈交鋒。
公投將於11月28日舉行，正好與全國地方選舉同一天。
這道由在野黨國民黨提出、8月在立法院以59比51的些微差距通過的題目，詢問選民是否支持以核能振興經濟，並廢除長期以來的「非核家園」政策。
為同意票辯護的國民黨立委牛煦庭堅稱，核能與再生能源應同步擴大。
他主張半導體和人工智慧產業需要可靠的基載電力，而高度依賴進口化石燃料，使台灣同時暴露在全球價格波動和可能的海上封鎖風險之下。
執政的民進黨陳培瑜反駁說，這次投票是多餘的，因為立委可以直接修改現行法律。
她重申政府對任何核能復甦的三項前提，也就是安全、可行的核廢料解決方案和社會共識，並指出經濟在整個能源轉型期間持續成長。
她指出，這次投票將花費約新台幣8億元。
自2025年5月最後一座反應爐停機以來，台灣就沒有產生任何核電。
當年舉行的一次公投同意票多於不同意票，但未達到規定的投票門檻。

paragraphs: Taiwan's energy debate intensified on 12 November as legislators from the two dominant parties confronted each other in a televised presentation ahead of a nuclear power referendum. The ballot, scheduled for 28 November, will be held in conjunction with nationwide local elections.

Initiated by the opposition Kuomintang (KMT) and endorsed by the legislature in August with a slender majority of 59 to 51, the referendum asks citizens whether they favour revitalising the economy through nuclear energy and abandoning the 'nuclear-free homeland' policy.

Advocating a yes vote, KMT legislator Niu Hsu-ting maintained that nuclear and renewable energy are complementary rather than competing. He argued that the island's chipmakers and AI developers rely on uninterrupted baseload supply, and that reliance on imported liquefied natural gas renders the grid vulnerable, since shipments could be disrupted by a maritime blockade whereas nuclear fuel can be stockpiled.

In response, Chen Pei-yu of the governing Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) dismissed the referendum as superfluous, observing that lawmakers retain the power to amend the relevant legislation. She emphasised that any revival of nuclear power remains contingent on three criteria: safety, a credible strategy for radioactive waste and broad social consensus. She also questioned whether the estimated NT$800 million cost was justified.
Since its final reactor was taken offline in May 2025, Taiwan has had no nuclear generation at all. Four additional presentations are scheduled before polling day.
sentZh: 11月12日，兩大主要政黨的立委在核能公投前的電視發表會上正面交鋒，使台灣的能源辯論更加激烈。
這次訂於11月28日的投票，將與全國地方選舉合併舉行。
這項公投由在野黨國民黨發起，8月在立法院以59比51的些微多數獲得通過，詢問公民是否贊成透過核能振興經濟並放棄「非核家園」政策。
主張投同意票的國民黨立委牛煦庭堅持認為，核能與再生能源是互補而非互相競爭的。
他認為，台灣的晶片製造商和人工智慧開發者仰賴不間斷的基載供電，而依賴進口液化天然氣會讓電網變得脆弱，因為運輸可能被海上封鎖打斷，核燃料卻可以儲備。
對此，執政的民進黨陳培瑜認為公投是多此一舉，並指出立委仍有權修改相關法律。
她強調，任何核能的恢復仍取決於三項標準：安全、可信的放射性廢料策略，以及廣泛的社會共識。
她也質疑估計約新台幣8億元的花費是否合理。
自從最後一座反應爐在2025年5月停機後，台灣就完全沒有核能發電。
投票日前還安排了四場發表會。

legislator.ex: The legislator spoke for ten minutes.

legislature.en: the group of people who make a country's laws

liquefied.ex: Liquefied gas is carried in special ships.

local.en: in or affecting a nearby small area

lot.ex: She drinks a lot of water every day.

maintained.ex: He maintains that the plan will work.

majority.en: more than half of a group
majority.ex: The majority of students passed the test.

making.ex: We are making good use of the new library.
making.hi: करते हुए (make use of: उपयोग करना)
making.zh: 做（make greater use of：更多利用）

margin.en: profit as a share of sales

maritime.ex: The navy protects maritime trade routes.

example.en: The navy patrols the country's maritime border every day.
example.zh: 海軍每天巡邏該國的海上邊界。

note.meaning: 海上的；與海洋或航運有關的。
note.usage: 多作形容詞置於名詞前，如 maritime security（海上安全）、maritime law。

noteHi.exampleTr: नौसेना हर दिन देश की समुद्री सीमा पर गश्त करती है।
noteHi.meaning: समुद्री; समुद्र या जहाज़रानी से जुड़ा।
noteHi.usage: संज्ञा से पहले विशेषण के रूप में: maritime security।

noteEs.exampleTr: La armada patrulla cada día la frontera marítima del país.
noteEs.meaning: marítimo; relacionado con el mar o la navegación.
noteEs.usage: Adjetivo antes del sustantivo: maritime security.

noteJa.exampleTr: 海軍は毎日その国の海上国境を巡回している。
noteJa.usage: 名詞の前に置く：maritime security（海上安全保障）。

noteKo.exampleTr: 해군은 매일 그 나라의 해상 국경을 순찰한다.
noteKo.usage: 명사 앞에 쓰는 형용사: maritime security(해상 안보).

noteEn.meaning: connected with the sea or ships.
noteEn.usage: Used before a noun, e.g. 'maritime security'.

may.ex: Kids may start school at four.
may.ja: …かもしれない；…することがある

million.ex: The city has over one million people.

month.ex: The rent is due each month.

most.en: used to make the superlative: to the greatest degree
most.ex: This is the most beautiful beach in Spain.

must.ex: You must wear a seatbelt in the car.

namely.ex: Two cities, namely Taipei and Tainan, were hit.

narrow.ex: We walked down a narrow street.

natural.ex: The river is the otters' natural home.

naval.ex: A naval ship arrived at the port.

needed.ex: More teachers are needed in rural areas.

night.en: the time when it is dark
night.ex: We saw the stars at night.

niu.en: a family name, as in Niu Hsu-ting

not.ex: I do not like cold tea.

noted.ex: She noted that prices were falling.
noted.zh: 注意到；指出（it should be noted：值得注意的是）

november.en: the eleventh month of the year

nuclear.en: using the energy from splitting atoms
nuclear.ex: The country has two nuclear power plants.

nuclear-free.ex: They hope to build a nuclear-free future.

observing.ex: She smiled, observing that it was late.

off.en: away from (off the coast); not allowed (off limits)
off.ex: The ship is off the coast of Hualien.

offline.ja: 停止して；オフラインで
offline.ex: The power station went offline for repairs.

on.ex: Voting will go on for nine days.

opposition.ex: The opposition voted against the bill.

out.en: points out: says, draws attention to
out.ex: She pointed out a mistake in my essay.

over.en: used to show control or influence
over.ex: Parents have control over the TV.

parallel.en: in parallel: at the same time
parallel.ex: The two tests ran in parallel.

part.ex: Cost is only part of the reason.

parties.ex: Both parties want people to vote.

pass.ex: The parade will pass the town hall at noon.

passed.ex: He passed the letter to his boss.

pei-yu.en: part of the name Chen Pei-yu

place.ex: New safety rules are now in place.

planned.ex: The planned trip was cancelled because of rain.

pointed.ex: He pointed to the rise in sales.

policy.ex: The new housing policy starts in May.

polling.en: the act of voting; "polling place" is where people vote
polling.ex: The polling station opens at seven.

potential.ex: We discussed potential problems with the plan.

power.ex: Big apps have power over small shops.

preconditions.ex: A ceasefire is a precondition for talks.

presentation.en: a talk that explains ideas to an audience
presentation.ex: She gave a short presentation on the new plan.

presentations.en: talks that explain ideas to an audience
presentations.ex: The students gave presentations in class.

prices.en: amounts of money paid for things

produced.ex: These cars are produced in Germany.

progressive.en: supporting new ideas and social change

put.ex: Put your name on the form.
put.zh: 放；（put on the website：放上網站）

question.en: something you ask to get an answer
question.ex: The teacher asked a difficult question.

questioned.ex: Experts questioned the safety of the bridge.

radioactive.en: giving off harmful energy from atoms
radioactive.ex: Radioactive waste must be stored very carefully.

rather.ex: It wasn't cheap. Rather, it was quite expensive.

reactor.en: the machine in a power plant that makes nuclear energy
reactor.ex: The old reactor was closed last year.

redundant.en: not needed because something else already does the job
redundant.ex: The extra step in the process is redundant.

referendum.en: a vote by all citizens on one question
referendum.ex: Ireland held a referendum on the issue.

reiterated.ex: She reiterated her support for the plan.

example.en: The minister reiterated her support for the plan.
example.zh: 部長重申她對該計畫的支持。

note.usage: reiterate a call/position/demand；比 repeat 更正式，多用於官方聲明。

noteHi.exampleTr: मंत्री ने योजना के लिए अपना समर्थन दोहराया।

noteEs.exampleTr: La ministra reiteró su apoyo al plan.
noteEs.usage: Más formal que repeat: reiterate a call/position.

noteJa.exampleTr: 大臣は計画への支持を改めて表明した。
noteJa.meaning: 繰り返し述べた；再表明した。
noteJa.usage: reiterate a call/position など公式発言で使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 장관은 그 계획에 대한 지지를 재차 밝혔다.
noteKo.usage: reiterate a call/position 등 공식 발언에 쓴다.

noteEn.meaning: said again, usually to make a point stronger.

relevant.ex: Please bring all relevant documents to the meeting.

reliable.en: able to be trusted to work well
reliable.ex: This is a reliable way to save money.

reliance.en: the state of depending on something
reliance.ex: Our reliance on cars causes pollution.

remains.ex: The shop remains open until late.

renewable.ex: Solar power is a renewable source of energy.

required.en: needed or demanded by a rule
required.ex: Passports are required for all travellers.

response.ex: The film got a warm response from critics.

retain.ex: The firm wants to retain its best workers.

return.en: going back to an earlier state
return.ex: The return to winter time brings dark evenings.

revitalising.en: giving new life or energy to something
revitalising.ex: The city is revitalising its old harbour area.

revival.ex: The town saw a revival of traditional crafts.

reviving.en: bringing something back to life or use
reviving.ex: They are reviving an old festival.

safe.ex: The water is safe to drink.

safety.ex: Wear a helmet for your safety.

said.ex: She said the shop was closed.

say.ex: Parents want more say in school rules.

says.ex: Experts say the plan will work.

scheduled.ex: The meeting is scheduled for Monday.

scrapping.en: getting rid of a plan or system
scrapping.ex: The company is scrapping its old phone service.

sectors.en: parts of an economy or society
sectors.ex: Jobs grew in the health and education sectors.

semiconductor.en: material used to make computer chips
semiconductor.ex: Taiwan has a large semiconductor industry.

series.en: Series A, B, C: stages of raising money for a young firm
series.ex: The start-up closed its Series A last year.

sharp.ex: There was a sharp rise in prices.

shipments.en: loads of goods sent from one place to another

ships.en: large boats that carry people or goods

shut.ex: Several cafés have shut for winter.

side.en: side effects: extra results, usually bad
side.ex: The plan had bad side effects.

simply.ex: Some crops simply cannot grow here.

slender.ex: The team won by a slender lead.

social.en: about society and people living together
social.ex: Poverty is a big social problem.

society.ex: She joined the society for engineers.

solution.en: a way to fix a problem
solution.ex: We finally found a solution to the leak.

sources.en: people who give information to reporters
sources.ex: Sources say the minister will resign.

stockpile.en: to store a large supply for later use
stockpile.ex: People began to stockpile rice before the storm.

stockpiled.en: stored in large amounts for later use
stockpiled.ex: Medicine was stockpiled for the winter.

stopped.ex: The rain stopped in the afternoon.

strategy.en: a plan to reach a long-term goal
strategy.ex: We need a clear strategy to save money.

sun.en: the star that gives the earth light and heat
sun.ex: The sun is very strong today.

superfluous.ex: Remove any superfluous words from your essay.

supply.ex: The supply of fresh water is limited.

support.ja: 支援（support staff：支援スタッフ）

taiwan.en: an island country in East Asia

take.en: to need a certain amount of time
take.ex: The trip can take three hours.

taken.ex: They have taken on a big task.

talked.ex: The teacher talked about the history of Rome.

talks.en: formal discussions to reach an agreement
talks.ex: Peace talks will start next month.

taxpayers.en: people who pay tax to the government
taxpayers.ex: The new bridge will cost taxpayers millions.

televised.ex: The televised debate lasted two hours.

there.ex: We went to the park and played there.

threshold.ex: Income above the threshold is taxed.

note.usage: 常見 exceed/reach a threshold；above the threshold。

example.en: Incomes above this threshold pay higher tax.
example.zh: 收入超過這個門檻的人繳較高的稅。

noteHi.usage: exceed/reach a threshold; above the threshold आम हैं।
noteHi.exampleTr: इस सीमा से अधिक आय वालों को ज़्यादा कर देना होता है।

noteEs.usage: Se usa exceed/reach a threshold; above the threshold.
noteEs.exampleTr: Los ingresos por encima de este umbral pagan más impuestos.

noteJa.usage: exceed/reach a threshold、above the threshold の形が多い。
noteJa.exampleTr: この基準を超える所得には高い税がかかる。

noteKo.usage: exceed/reach a threshold, above the threshold 형태가 흔하다.
noteKo.exampleTr: 이 기준을 넘는 소득에는 더 높은 세금이 붙는다.

noteEn.meaning: a level or limit at which something changes.

through.ex: They bought it through a special deal.

too.ex: The coffee is too hot to drink.

took.en: began a job; caused damage (took a toll)
took.ex: She took up the job in May.
took.zh: 就任（took up）；造成（took a toll）

traded.en: exchanged words or things with each other
traded.ex: The two leaders traded insults on TV.

transition.en: the change from one state to another
transition.ex: The transition to electric cars will take years.

turnout.en: the number of people who vote or attend
turnout.ex: Turnout was higher than last year.

tv.ex: The TV is in the kitchen.

uninterrupted.ex: Hospitals need an uninterrupted power supply.

urged.en: strongly asked someone to do something
urged.ex: The doctor urged him to stop smoking.

used.en: put into service for a purpose
used.ex: The old bricks were used again.

using.ex: Using a map helped us find the hotel.

example.en: Solar power is a viable option for farms.
example.zh: 太陽能對農場是可行的選擇。

noteHi.exampleTr: सौर ऊर्जा खेतों के लिए व्यवहार्य विकल्प है।
noteHi.usage: option, plan, product के साथ; संज्ञा viability।

noteEs.exampleTr: La energía solar es una opción viable para granjas.
noteEs.usage: Con option, plan, product; sustantivo viability.

noteJa.exampleTr: 太陽光は農場にとって実行可能な選択肢だ。
noteJa.usage: option, plan, product と使う。名詞は viability。

noteKo.usage: option, plan, product와 쓰며 명사는 viability.

view.ex: In my view, the plan is too costly.
view.zh: 看法（in their view：在他們看來）

note.usage: 形容地區、市場、局勢；a volatile region/market。

noteHi.exampleTr: तेल की क़ीमतें बहुत अस्थिर हैं।

noteEs.exampleTr: El precio del petróleo es muy volátil.
noteEs.usage: Para regiones, mercados; a volatile market.

noteJa.exampleTr: 原油価格は非常に不安定だ。
noteJa.meaning: 不安定な；変わりやすい。
noteJa.usage: 地域・市場に使う。a volatile region。

noteEn.meaning: likely to change suddenly or become violent.

vote.en: to choose formally in an election

voted.en: made a choice in a vote
voted.ex: Most members voted for the plan.

voters.en: people who vote in an election

votes.ex: The bill won by ten votes.

vulnerable.ex: Old computers are vulnerable to viruses.
vulnerable.ja: 脆弱な；攻撃されやすい

example.en: Coastal towns are vulnerable to flooding.
example.zh: 沿海城鎮容易遭受洪水侵襲。

noteHi.usage: be vulnerable to sth आम प्रयोग है।
noteHi.exampleTr: तटीय शहर बाढ़ के प्रति असुरक्षित हैं।

noteEs.usage: Se usa be vulnerable to algo.
noteEs.exampleTr: Los pueblos costeros son vulnerables a las inundaciones.

noteJa.meaning: 弱い；影響を受けやすい。
noteJa.usage: be vulnerable to ～ の形が多い。
noteJa.exampleTr: 沿岸の町は洪水に弱い。

wants.ex: She wants a quiet place to study.

warned.ex: Experts warned of a hot summer.

waste.en: things thrown away because no longer needed
waste.ex: Put food waste in the brown bin.

weeks.ex: The plan will be ready in a few weeks.

went.ex: The bill went to parliament last week.

whether.en: used to express a choice (if or not)

will.en: used to talk about the future
will.ex: The new bridge will open next year.

wind.ex: The wind was very strong last night.

won.ex: Our team won the cup last year.

workable.en: able to work well in practice
workable.ex: We need a workable plan by Friday.

would.ex: A new park would help the town.
